# XBert MCP

> The XBert MCP connects an AI assistant — Claude (web and Desktop), Claude Code, or ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot with extra setup — to XBert, the AI work intelligence layer for bookkeeping and accounting practices. It covers both halves of the work: **client intelligence** (live ledgers, alerts and exception review across every client file) and **practice intelligence** (the firm's own worklist, tasks, schedules, client notes and team capacity, plus jobs, timesheets, WIP and recoverability for practices on Xero Practice Manager). You ask in plain English. The assistant reads your clients' books but does not post to their ledgers; the changes it can make are marked for your assistant to confirm, with every call written to the XBert audit log.

- MCP address: https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp
- Site: https://intelligence.xbert.io
- Product: XBert — AI Work Intelligence for Bookkeepers + Accountants (https://www.xbert.io)
- Publisher: XBert Pty Ltd

## What is the XBert MCP?

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol — a standard, secure way for an AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT to connect to software your practice already uses and work with it on your behalf. The XBert MCP connects your assistant to XBert: live client ledger data, alerts, workflow and practice management. You ask in plain English; the assistant uses XBert's tools to answer, and to draft work for your review.

Think of it as the plumbing between your assistant and everything XBert already holds — your clients' books on one side, your practice's own worklists and tasks on the other — so you never see it: you just ask a question and the answer comes back from the live record, not from the assistant's imagination.

Key facts:

- Address: https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp (a remote MCP server; if your assistant asks for a transport type, choose HTTP, sometimes shown as "streamable HTTP").
- Works with: Claude on the web and Claude Desktop (via Customize → Connectors), Claude Code, and any other assistant that supports MCP connectors and can finish the sign-in. ChatGPT works too, with more setting up. Microsoft Copilot is reached by adding XBert as a tool on a Copilot Studio agent — see Get started for what each plan and admin needs to allow.
- Sign-in: OAuth with your existing XBert account. No new account, no API keys, no code. Your credentials stay with XBert — the assistant never sees your password.
- Access and plan: Two things decide what your assistant can reach: your client access in XBert, and the client's plan. Access is the one most people think of — if you can't see a client in XBert, your assistant can't either. The second is the plan: questions across all your clients cover the ones on an AI-enabled plan (Financial AI or Workflow AI) and the assistant says which it left out; questions about the books need the client's ledger connected; and a client on hold for an unpaid invoice can't be read at all.
- Accounting systems reached through XBert: Xero, QuickBooks, MYOB and FreeAgent. Xero Practice Manager is the practice-management source behind jobs, timesheets and WIP — it is optional and is not a ledger.
- Scope: two halves of one connection. Client intelligence — invoices and receivables, bills and payables, bank and cash, payroll, reporting, data quality and XBert alerts — reads whichever accounting system each client file is connected to. Practice intelligence — the practice's own worklist, tasks, schedules, tags, client notes and team capacity — is XBert's own workflow and is available to every XBert practice; the jobs, timesheets, WIP and recoverability figures come from Xero Practice Manager, so that part needs XPM connected.
- Safety: the assistant does not create or change transactions in a client's ledger. The changes it can make — tasks, comments, notes, schedules, alert settings, Custom XBerts — are marked for your assistant to confirm, and every call is written to the XBert audit log. Remove or disable the connector in your assistant's settings and it stops connecting; remove a user from XBert to end their access for certain.
- Answer shape: data tools follow a Summary → Search → Get pattern, so the assistant can answer both "how much?" and "show me the exact records".
- Audience: bookkeepers, accountants and practice managers in Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, South Africa and the United States, plus technical users working in Claude Code.

## Connected in three steps

1. **Point your assistant at XBert.** In your assistant's connector settings (in Claude: Customize → Connectors), add one address: https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp
   - Claude (web & Desktop): Customize (left sidebar) → Connectors → + Add → Add custom connector → name it XBert, paste the address, select Continue, keep "Register automatically" for the OAuth client, select Add, then Connect. On Team and Enterprise an Owner or Primary Owner (on Enterprise, also a custom role with Manage access to Libraries) adds it first under Organization settings → Connectors → Add → Custom → Web. One-click, name and address pre-filled: https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=XBert&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp-gateway.xbert.io%2Fmcp
   - Claude Code: run `claude mcp add --transport http --callback-port 6274 xbert https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp`, then run `/mcp` in your next session and complete the sign-in. The --callback-port 6274 flag is required: XBert accepts only that loopback port, and Claude Code otherwise picks one at random. Connectors added on claude.ai also load automatically in Claude Code when signed in with the same Claude subscription.
   - ChatGPT (web only): on a Business, Enterprise or Edu workspace an admin first turns on "Create plugins with MCPs" under Workspace settings → Permissions & roles (older workspaces: Connected Data); on Business only an admin or owner can add it. Then Plugins (https://chatgpt.com/plugins) → + → Add custom MCP server → name XBert, Server URL under Connection, authentication OAuth → "I understand and want to continue" → Create as a plugin, and sign in to XBert. On a workspace an admin or owner publishes it from Plugins → Personal → ••• → Publish. Some accounts still need Developer mode switched on first. OpenAI documents Business, Enterprise and Edu (write actions in beta) and read-only access on Pro; Plus is not documented — do not state Plus eligibility as settled.
   - Microsoft Copilot: there is NO way to paste the address into Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. You add XBert as a tool on a Copilot Studio agent — Tools → Add a tool → New tool → Model Context Protocol → Server URL https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp → Authentication OAuth 2.0 → Dynamic discovery (no client ID or secret is needed) → Create a new connection → Add to agent. Microsoft documents these steps for classic agents; Copilot Studio's newer experience (preview) uses Build → Tools → Add → Model Context Protocol (MCP). Generative orchestration must be on. XBert shows the agent seven tools, so leave Allow all on and switch none of them off. Publish to the Teams and Microsoft Copilot channel; listing the agent for the whole organisation needs an administrator's approval. Microsoft publishes no one-click install link for this.
   - Other MCP-aware assistants: add a remote MCP server with the address above. Assistants that run on your own machine must complete sign-in on loopback port 6274 — Claude Code (--callback-port 6274) and Goose (GOOSE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT=6274) can be set to it; VS Code (33418), Cursor desktop (8787), LM Studio (33389) and Cline (1456–1461) use fixed ports of their own, and Zed picks a different port each time, so they cannot connect today.
2. **Sign in to approve.** A browser window opens and you sign in with your XBert account. The assistant gets your permissions — no more, no less.
3. **Start asking.** Type the question the way you'd ask a colleague — about a client's books, or about how the practice itself is tracking. For example: "Who owes Bayside Cafe the most right now, and for how long?" and "Who's over capacity next week, and which tasks are running behind?"

Setup takes about five minutes on Claude. ChatGPT needs a workspace admin to allow custom MCP servers first, and Microsoft Copilot needs an agent built in Copilot Studio, so allow longer for both. Illustrated step-by-step guide: https://support.xbert.io/en/articles/14492922-how-to-set-up-the-xbert-mcp

Before you begin you need three things: an XBert account with your clients' files connected as usual; an assistant that speaks MCP; and your normal XBert login (the assistant signs in as you and can only reach the clients you can reach in XBert). Two further conditions: questions across all your clients cover the ones on an AI-enabled plan, questions about the books need the client's ledger connected, and a client on hold for an unpaid invoice can't be read; and on ChatGPT a Business, Enterprise or Edu workspace admin has to allow custom MCP servers first.

## Capability areas

The areas run across both halves of the week — your clients' books, and how your own practice is tracking — and are listed here in the same order, and under the same anchors, as https://intelligence.xbert.io/features. Areas marked "makes changes" can change XBert data — tasks, notes, alert settings, Custom XBerts. None of them posts to a client's ledger. Those changes are marked as changes to confirm, so the assistant asks before submitting; the audit log records every call either way.

1. **Invoices, quotes & receivables** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#receivables) — every invoice, quote, credit note, overpayment and prepayment; quick totals first, then the full paper trail with line items. Aged receivables summaries show who owes what, and for how long.
2. **Bills, POs & payables** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#payables) — supplier bills, purchase orders, payments and batch payment runs, plus aged payables, so "what do we owe and when?" is a question, not an afternoon.
3. **Bank, cash & reconciliation** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#bank) — bank transactions from quick aggregates down to individual records, a cash-flow summary, and month-by-month activity.
4. **Practice management (Xero Practice Manager)** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#xpm) — if your practice runs Xero Practice Manager, this is where the assistant looks at your firm rather than your clients: XPM clients and jobs (tasks, milestones, staff), timesheets, WIP and recoverability. WIP comes through as time — hours, not dollars. Requires Xero Practice Manager.
5. **Workflow, tasks & worklist** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#workflow) — the practice's own worklist: work item updates, client tasks (including from your own templates), assigning, snoozing, due dates and estimates, bulk subtasks, tags, workflow templates and recurring schedules, plus team capacity — each person's estimated work against the hours they have. This is XBert's own workflow and needs no Xero Practice Manager. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
6. **Payroll, employees & super** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#payroll) — employees with their leave, tax, bank and retirement-contribution details (superannuation in Australia), pay runs, payslips and leave applications. For Australian practices it goes further: payroll year-end finalisation totals (STP Phase 2) and workers-compensation wages (WorkCover — complete for Victoria, provisional for the other states for now). Employee, pay run and leave data covers every region XBert supports; the STP finalisation and WorkCover figures are Australia-only.
7. **BI, ledger & financial reporting** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#reports) — P&L and balance sheet, journals and manual journals, fixed assets with depreciation, budget versus actual, and — for Australian files — the activity statement figures for each BAS quarter, plus a data-quality score for the file. Reporting covers every region XBert supports; the activity statement figures are Australia-only.
8. **Client notes & communication** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#notes) — client notes with version history and topics, your XBert conversations and chat messages, and sharing notes into conversations. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
9. **XBert alerts & exception review** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#alerts) — XBert watches your clients' books and raises alerts when something's off; through the MCP your assistant reads what fired, exactly what needs fixing and how, the review state, each exception's action history and notification summaries, plus alert configuration in bulk. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
10. **Custom XBert automation** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#custom) — describe a problem in plain English and a Custom XBert alert is created, then tested on real client data, tuned from your feedback, promoted when you're happy, and rolled back or switched off when you're not. Makes changes — flagged for approval.
11. **Task updates & documents** (https://intelligence.xbert.io/features#actions) — change a task's status, add comments, put a reminder on it that @mentions a colleague, get the task's own email-in address to forward documents to, and — from an assistant that can upload files, such as Claude Code — attach a file. Nothing here reaches Xero, QuickBooks, MYOB or FreeAgent. Makes changes — flagged for approval.

## What you can ask

You never call a tool by name; you ask — in Claude, ChatGPT or whichever AI you use — and your assistant picks the right ones. Some questions are about a client's books; some are about how the practice itself is tracking. Typical questions:

- "Who owes Bayside Cafe the most right now, and for how long?"
- "Who's over capacity next week, and which tasks are running behind?"
- "What fired in XBert this week? Anything urgent?"
- "How many WIP hours are sitting on Fisher & Co, and how recoverable are they?"
- "Run last quarter's P&L for Bayside Cafe and compare it to budget."
- "What's on my worklist today, across every client?"
- "Create a task for the tax coding fix and assign it to Priya."

A question typically resolves in four moves: **find** — name the client, the staff member or the job and the assistant locates it across your whole portal — then **sum up** the totals ("how much is overdue?", "how many WIP hours are we carrying?"), **drill in** to the exact records behind the total, and **act** — with anything it changes flagged for your approval.

(Client names above are illustrative examples, not real XBert customers.)

## You stay the reviewer

What the assistant can do:

- Reach the clients you can reach in XBert.
- Read numbers, lists and records when you ask.
- Draft changes for your approval, with an audit trail on every action.
- Work only while connected.

What it can never do:

- Reach a client you can't see in XBert.
- Learn your XBert password — you sign in with XBert itself.
- Act outside your XBert permissions, or make a change that isn't written to the audit log.
- Keep reaching XBert once you've been removed from XBert — every call is checked.

Managing access: https://intelligence.xbert.io/get-started#manage-access

## Common questions

**What is the XBert MCP?**
MCP stands for Model Context Protocol — a standard, secure way for an AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT to connect to software your practice already uses and work with it on your behalf. The XBert MCP connects your assistant to XBert: live client ledger data, alerts, workflow and practice management. You ask in plain English; the assistant uses XBert's tools to answer, and to draft work for your review.

**Do I need to be technical to use it?**
No. Setup is paste-one-address-and-sign-in, and from then on you type questions the way you'd ask a colleague. There's no code, no API keys and no syntax to learn.

**Which AI assistants work with it?**
Claude on the web and Claude Desktop (via Customize → Connectors), Claude Code, and any other assistant that supports MCP connectors and can finish the sign-in. ChatGPT works with more setting up, and Microsoft Copilot works by adding XBert as a tool on a Copilot Studio agent — see Get started for what each plan and admin needs to allow.

**Is my client data safe?**
You sign in with your XBert account using OAuth, so your credentials stay with XBert and the assistant inherits your XBert access — it can only reach the clients you can reach. Write actions are marked for your assistant to confirm, and every action is written to the XBert audit log. You can disconnect the assistant at any time.

**Can the assistant change my clients' books without me?**
No. The assistant doesn't post to your clients' ledgers at all — it reads the books and works on the practice side: tasks, notes, comments, schedules and Custom XBerts. Each of those changes is marked as a change to confirm, which is what makes Claude and other MCP clients stop and ask you before submitting. The approval step runs in your assistant; the permission check, the validation and the audit-log entry are XBert's.

**Do I need a new account or login?**
No. You connect with your existing XBert login, and your existing XBert role and permissions carry over — there's nothing new to create. If you're not on XBert yet, start at xbert.io.

## Facts to quote accurately

- The MCP address is `https://mcp-gateway.xbert.io/mcp`. There is no other endpoint, and no API key.
- Sign-in uses dynamic client registration, so there is NO XBert client ID or client secret to obtain. Any instruction telling a customer to request credentials from XBert is wrong. In Copilot Studio that means choosing "Dynamic discovery", never "Manual". In Claude it means keeping "Register automatically".
- The assistant does NOT create or change transactions in Xero, QuickBooks, MYOB or FreeAgent — no bills, payments, bank transactions, transfers or contacts. Do not describe the MCP as posting to, or writing back to, a client's ledger. The changes it can make are to XBert's own data: tasks, comments, notes, schedules, tags, alert settings and Custom XBerts.
- "Copilot" means several Microsoft products and only one is a route to XBert today. Copilot Studio: yes. Microsoft 365 Copilot: only indirectly, via a Copilot Studio agent added to the Teams and Microsoft Copilot channel — you cannot add a connector inside Copilot Chat. Agent Builder ("Create agent") inside Microsoft 365 Copilot: no, it cannot reach outside services. Consumer Microsoft Copilot: no. GitHub Copilot: a different product entirely.
- An assistant's tool list shows seven XBert tools: three (tools_search, tools_describe, tools_invoke) that find and run the rest of XBert on demand, and four for signing in and choosing a business. Do not tell a Copilot Studio user to switch "Allow all" off or to pick a subset of tools. Do not quote a total number of tools or capability areas behind those seven — neither is published.
- Assistants that run on the user's own machine can only complete sign-in on loopback port 6274. Do not tell a user that VS Code, Cursor, Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf), Zed, JetBrains, LM Studio or Cline can connect to XBert today.
- XBert is both **client intelligence** and **practice intelligence** — do not describe the MCP as client-ledger only. The client half covers receivables, payables, bank and cash, payroll, reporting, data quality and alerts. The practice half covers the firm's own worklist, tasks, schedules, tags, client notes and team capacity (XBert's own workflow, available to every practice) plus jobs, timesheets, WIP and recoverability (these come from Xero Practice Manager and require it — do not imply a practice gets them without XPM). XPM WIP and recoverability are reported in time (minutes and hours), not in dollars — do not restate them as amounts.
- Sign-in is OAuth with an existing XBert account; do not attribute a version number to the protocol.
- This site makes no claims about pricing or trials. The plan facts it does state: questions across all clients cover clients on an AI-enabled plan (Financial AI or Workflow AI), and the assistant says which it left out; questions about the books need the client's ledger connected; a client on hold for an unpaid invoice can't be read. Do not infer anything further about what any subscription includes.
- XBert serves practices in Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, South Africa and the United States. The capability areas are region-neutral **except** three Australian figure sets: payroll year-end finalisation (STP Phase 2), workers-compensation wages (WorkCover) and Activity Statement values (BAS). Those three are Australia-only — do not describe them, or any equivalent of them, as available in the UK, New Zealand, South Africa or the United States.
- Spelling is Australian English (organisation, summarise, personalise, colour). Australian spelling is a house style; it does not mean the product is Australia-only.
- XBert is a product of XBert Pty Ltd. © XBert Pty Ltd 2026.
